summary: Persistent ordered consumption addresses proven unbounded task creation and absent lifecycle fences. It requires durable loss signaling, in-flight capacity ownership, and epoch checks at bridge mutation. A particular intermittent failure was not reproduced.

findings.claim: Each callback spawns an unstructured Task: outstanding raw payloads are unbounded and callback order is unfenced. receive can restore available after stop/crash. These are source-proven hazards; attribution of a specific intermittent failure remains inference.
findings.recommendation: Use one persistent consumer and synchronous FIFO admission. For concurrent callbacks define order as inbox-lock admission unless runtime guarantees stronger order; do not assume sequence sorting can safely wait for missing events.

findings.claim: Sequence advances before filtering, correctly preserving contiguous excluded events. But allowed 1, excluded 3, allowed 4 loses the gap. Invalid input also advances sequence before normalization throws; try? hides this. lastSequence + 1 can overflow.
findings.recommendation: Keep raw sequence accounting through filtering and pending discontinuity until an admitted event carries it. Publish loss status even without later events. Define invalid-input loss semantics and use overflow-safe comparison.

findings.claim: A bufferingNewest(1) signal cannot own payload/loss state. Dequeue-time release or restart clearing in-flight reservations violates bounds. Existing bridge byte estimates omit variable fields; coalescing bypasses replacement-size checks.
findings.recommendation: Reserve count/bytes at admission, releasing exactly once after commit/discard, including old-epoch in-flight data. Bound retained variable fields or document estimates; reject oversize input before retention. Keep drops in bounded scalar state and wake on rejection. Drain/recheck under coherent locking to avoid lost wakes; create no task or loss record per rejection.

findings.claim: Unserialized start/stop/crash permits retained callbacks, synchronous callbacks during start, and stale transitions. Later available can mask overload; old failure/stop can overwrite a new session. Checking epoch only before await does not prevent stale commit.
findings.recommendation: Assign unique epochs; close admission synchronously and reject captured old epochs. Serialize runtime lifecycle and fence all async success/failure/completion paths. Validate epoch atomically with sequence/buffer/status mutation; revalidate after any test-gate await. Await invalidation before stop returns. Prevent old epoch reactivation, activation-time loss, old worker cleanup affecting new state, and observer-retaining worker cycles.

findings.claim: Existing delivery coverage sleeps 20 ms and lacks held delivery, retained callback, raw-inbox overflow, and restart fencing tests.
findings.recommendation: Barrier-ack event 1 at consumer, hold it, emit distinct noncoalescing 2/3, release and await commit acknowledgments before order/confidence assertions. Test allowed 1/excluded 2/allowed 3 and allowed 1/excluded 3/allowed 4 separately. Hold event 1, fill tiny count/byte limits, overflow, assert in-flight accounting, release and await loss acknowledgment without another event. Retain handler across stop and prove rejection. Hold old delivery across stop/restart, emit new input, release old and assert no old sequence/buffer/status mutation or false gap; repeat crash/delayed startup failure. Use explicit commit/rejection/loss acknowledgments, not sleeps, polling, or actor reads as flushes.
